scale.pass: The report satisfies the dimension for this fixture.
scale.partial: The report provides some value but has a material limitation.
scale.fail: The report misses or contradicts the dimension.
scale.not_applicable: The condition contains no retrieved knowledge to assess.

method_note: Input values, validator and release outcome are machine-checkable. Retrieval relevance, knowledge utilisation, audience suitability, action safety and relationship-level uncertainty were manually reviewed against the saved prompt, retrieved text and output. These labels are an auditable case review, not validated automatic metric scores.

records.evidence: Values and Low-risk meaning were preserved; actions were safe and mostly delegated, but candidate causes came from model knowledge rather than supplied evidence.
The retrieved passage was dominated by overheating and workshop fault lists despite a low-temperature Low-risk pattern; the prompt caution prevented most irrelevant material from entering the report.
The report used the safe coolant-level check and delegated infrared measurement to a mechanic, although fault retrieval remained over-broad.
Owner observations were separated from mechanic checks and the hot-component warning was retained; retrieval relevance was unchanged.
The report stated that readings were within range and kept the Low-risk interpretation cautious; the proposed inspection was assigned to a professional.
Retrieved component function and candidate causes were relevant and were used without directing specialist procedures to the owner.
The report used retrieved scan-tool guidance, but asked a non-technical owner to connect a scan tool, interpret PID behaviour and clean connector contacts.
Technical scanning and wiring checks were redirected to a mechanic; a duplicated word remains a separate language-quality defect.
The report preserved the Medium risk and normal listed signals, used cautious candidate causes and delegated diagnosis.
Component-specific wear, wiring and connector alternatives were traceable to relevant retrieved knowledge; 'could indicate' was valid hedging despite the legacy evaluator penalty.
The report converted workshop guidance into a direct request for the owner to inspect the pedal-sensor harness connector.
The owner was asked to observe warnings and pedal response while connector inspection and scanning were assigned to a mechanic.
The report repeated both High current risk and a 0.31% probability of crossing the High-risk threshold but did not identify or resolve their contradiction.
Relevant circuit and connector causes were used, but the owner was asked to inspect a sensor and harness; the High-risk/threshold contradiction remained.

Cause retrieval was relevant, but action retrieval only proposed replacing MAF or ECM and was appropriately not copied. The output still directed sensor inspection to the owner and missed the risk contradiction.
Technical checks were correctly delegated and unsupported replacement was avoided, but owner-safe transformation could not repair irrelevant action retrieval or the risk contradiction.
The abnormal pressure reading was preserved, but High current risk was presented alongside a low future threshold-crossing probability without explaining the inconsistency.
Relevant MAP function, wiring and vacuum-leak causes were used and mechanic verification was recommended; the risk contradiction remained.

The retrieved action was conditional on turbo engines without matching vehicle context. The report mainly used cause knowledge and asked the owner to check vacuum hoses; the risk contradiction remained.
Sensor, hose and wiring checks were delegated to a mechanic, but the conditional retrieval and risk contradiction were not resolved.
